tagline: Down the Mohawk Valley, where the Revolution came through.
intro: The byway starts at Port Ontario on Lake Ontario and runs inland through Pulaski, Williamstown and Camden to Rome. From there it largely follows the Mohawk River down its valley, through Utica, Ilion, Little Falls, Canajoharie and Amsterdam to Schenectady. The mapped line stops there, and the official byway carries on to Albany, 158 miles from the lake.

In the Revolution the Mohawk was a critical east-west artery for trade, settlement and the movement of troops. In August 1777 a British army that had come in from Canada by way of Lake Ontario laid siege to Fort Stanwix, and the militia marching to relieve it was ambushed at Oriskany.

moments.title: Fort Stanwix
moments.text: In Rome a reconstructed fort stands on the Oneida Carry, the old portage between the Mohawk and the waters to Lake Ontario, with three short trails circling it.

moments.title: Oriskany Battlefield
moments.text: On a rise above the Mohawk bottomlands an 1884 obelisk marks where the wounded General Herkimer rallied and directed his militia, who fought in pairs, one firing while the other reloaded.

moments.title: Little Falls
moments.text: The Mohawk drops 45 feet in less than a mile through a rocky defile here, and Lock 17 of the Erie Canal, 40.5 feet high, does the work of three older locks.
